notes: The code changes match the reference exactly: both zip and squashfs skip symlinks without --links and log a notice naming the flag, NewObject agrees with List, and link objects read back their target with range/seek clamped. The tests cover the zip and squashfs symlink paths, a regular member named with the .rclonelink suffix, and an end-to-end hostile-archive escape. The docs addition is relevant but goes slightly beyond what was strictly needed.

The production code matches the reference for both zip and squashfs: links are skipped with a notice naming the flag unless --links is set, NewObject agrees with List, and link reads honour range/seek. The tests cover the squashfs flag on/off, a regular member named .rclonelink, and an end-to-end hostile-archive escape. The docs addition is relevant but goes slightly beyond the minimal fix.

The production code matches the reference fix: it records the placeholder names from the checked CEL AST and treats an expression as a response condition only if it reads status, header or latency placeholders, or a placeholder name known only at evaluation time. The tests cover every case the maintainers agreed on, including the shorthand vs ph() forms, escaped literals, the prefix-lookalike name, the upstream host placeholder and the dynamic name, with end-to-end retry checks.

The non-test code is identical to the reference: it records CEL placeholder names at provision time, treats literal response placeholders, the header prefix, and dynamic names as response conditions, and adds thorough unit and integration tests covering every edge case the maintainers listed.

The visible non-test changes match the reference exactly: the exemplar timestamp is tracked in both appenders, gcSeries and stripeSeries.gc keep the series identity while releasing persisted chunks and the appender, and mmap-ready accounting is handled. The WAL replay update was cut off in the truncated diff, but the passing replay-then-recompact test suggests it is present. The tests are thorough, covering ordinary, selected and stale compaction, snapshots, both appender versions, chunk-metric accounting, concurrent appends and the cutoff boundary. The one unneeded change is a refactor of the colliding-series test helper.

The non-test changes match the reference fix: it tracks exemplar timestamps under the series lock in both appenders and both replay paths, keeps the series identity in head GC and gcSeries while releasing chunks, the appender and mmap-ready state, and keeps empty retained series out of the min-time calculation; the tests are thorough and cover all three compaction modes, both appender APIs, snapshot replay, chunk metrics and concurrent appends, though a small unrelated-looking refactor of the colliding-series test helper is included.

The source change matches the reference exactly: it closes the dup'd file, guards double-close with ErrClosed, serializes Close under the map mutex, unlinks only on the last reference, and skips abstract sockets. The added tests cover each review requirement (immediate close and unlink, refcounting, double close, concurrent close/relisten, abstract-socket sentinel) for both stream and datagram sockets; one test calls reuseUnixSocket without holding the mutex, which is harmless in a single-threaded test.

The source change matches the reference exactly: it closes the dup'd fd, makes `Close` idempotent and return `net.ErrClosed` on a repeat, holds the lock across the refcount change and unlink, and guards abstract sockets. The tests cover immediate close and unlink, refcounted reuse, double close, concurrent close and relisten for both unix and unixgram, and abstract sockets; the only blemish is that the abstract-socket test writes a sentinel file into the package directory.

C1 generalizes prefix stripping to any first component, adds rename/copy-to fallbacks and forces strippable prefixes on lazygit's own diffs (including the extra stash-show-to-apply pipe); unlike the reference it also overrides the user's diff.mnemonicPrefix, a defensible but user-visible design choice. The truncated diff hides the diff --git splitting logic and any new parser tests, though the hidden tests pass.

Generalizes prefix stripping and adds the rename/copy-to fallback like the reference, but also forces diff.mnemonicPrefix=false on every displayed diff (overriding a user preference the parser no longer needs overridden) and touches SaveStagedChanges, which is defensible but beyond the reported bug; the diff --git split logic is truncated, though the hidden tests pass.

Fixes both symptoms: callers stay Cancelling while a direct child is unfinished, and concurrency waiters are re-checked when no job was updated. But it re-implements the caller's status in cancelOneJob and rewrites a row the child's cascade has usually already set to Cancelling. On MySQL/MariaDB that same-value update reports 0 affected rows, which may trigger the n==0 failure path or drop the caller from the returned list. The reference sidesteps this by just re-reading the caller. The new end-to-end handshake and force-cancel tests are good, though the service test sets ParentJobID from a not-yet-inserted caller ID (always 0).

The fix is correct but takes a different route from the reference: cancelOneJob now writes a reusable caller as Cancelling while any direct child is not done, and the deepest-first order makes this work at any nesting depth, and a run whose jobs are already all done now re-emits its concurrency groups so blocked runs can start. Weaknesses: it adds a second aggregation rule and an extra child query instead of re-reading the cascaded status, it may drop the caller from the returned updated-jobs list when the write changes nothing, and it re-emits even when the run status did not change. The tests are strong: a nested-caller handshake through UpdateTaskByState, plus a force-cancel test showing the blocked waiter is woken.

The core fix matches the reference: it adds `Close` to the interface, reconnects in `Get`/`Walk`, resets USM state when reconnecting a closed connection, and closes the connection on gather failures. However, it restores any configured engine ID instead of forcing fresh discovery, which departs from the maintainer spec. It also adds private fields to the exported `GosnmpWrapper`, which breaks positional struct literals and likely explains the hidden-test and suite failures. It also edits the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (path workaround plus a `Log` field) and surfaces extra close errors; the new tests are otherwise solid.

The core recovery works for the reported case: the snmp input closes the agent's connection on any field or table failure, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect a closed connection, and reconnect clears the stale engine ID, boots and time (and, beyond the reference, the stale `ContextEngineID`). However, it adds stored-state fields to the exported `GosnmpWrapper` struct and restores preconfigured engine parameters on reconnect instead of always forcing the fresh discovery the spec requires, which likely explains the failing hidden test; it also edits the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` and adds close-error reporting to the accumulator, which nobody asked for.
